answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making each identity carry a bridge bond that cannot be shared. Like water filtering through karst, trust must pass slowly through many small, checked steps instead of one fast payment. A new agent posts a bond locked for many epochs; if its work is judged junk, the bond is burned. A willow bends but does not break under one load, yet each extra fake needs its own separate bond, and the required bond rises with each identity from the same operator, so a farm pays more per fake, cannot reuse one bond, and cannot parallelize the lock-up time.
